sop_title: NETCINST 4200.4A Enclosure (1): Government-Wide Commercial Purchase Card Program (GCPC) Internal Operating Procedures
summary: This SOP covers the NETC purchase card program from end to end: appointing cardholders, getting funding and approvals, buying and receiving goods and services, reconciling and certifying monthly statements, handling disputes, fraud and lost cards, closing accounts when cardholders leave, and running internal and external program reviews. It is run by Cardholders (CHs), Approving/Certifying Officials (AO/CO), the A/OPC (GCPC Program Manager, N4), N8 as funds manager, requesting divisions and departments, CITIBANK, and higher-level reviewers (HA, PMR Team, CCPMD).

steps.action: Nominates the cardholder to the A/OPC by email or memo; the A/OPC is notified of the new participant.
steps.source_quote: The CH will be nominated by the requesting department by email or memo.

steps.action: Completes initial training (DAU CLG0001, online DON GCPC role training, DoD Ethics, activity IOP training; CLG 006 for COs and D/AOs).
steps.source_quote: All GCPC program participants will complete initial training before assuming program responsibility.

steps.action: Provides a copy of all training certificates to the A/OPC.
steps.source_quote: A copy of all training certificates will be provided to the A/OPC.

steps.action: Acknowledges responsibility for and understanding of reference (a) and this instruction.
steps.source_quote: The CH will acknowledge the responsibility

steps.action: Appoints the CH by delegation of authority letter, which sets the single purchase, monthly CH and monthly office limits.
steps.source_quote: be appointed delegation of authority

steps.action: Appoints the CH on SF 1402 (Certificate of Appointment) specifying spending limits and authorized transaction types.
steps.source_quote: The CH will be appointed using SF 1402 (Certificate of Appointment) if their procurement authority exceeds the micro-purchase threshold.

steps.action: Coordinates the card application and issuance and submits dollar limits and authorized merchant codes to CITIBANK.
steps.source_quote: The A/OPC submits changes to dollar limitations or authorized merchant codes to CITIBANK.

steps.action: Incorporates merchant category authorization codes into the card when it is issued.
steps.output: Issued card with merchant category codes
steps.source_quote: authorization codes are incorporated in the card by CCPMD

steps.action: Issues LOAs for each purchase type (supplies, equipment, communication, services, printing) to N4, which serves as AO, before the fiscal year.
steps.source_quote: Lines of Accounting (LOAs) are issued for each type of purchase and provided to N4 prior to starting a new fiscal year.

steps.action: Issues staff training LOAs to departments before the fiscal year.
steps.source_quote: LOAs are issued to departments prior to the start of the fiscal year.

steps.action: Discusses centrally managed requirements with department heads or program managers before the fiscal year.
steps.source_quote: Requirements are discussed with department heads or program managers prior to starting a new fiscal year.

steps.action: Emails a centrally managed purchase request to N8.
steps.source_quote: Requests are emailed to N8.

steps.action: Forwards an unusual or questionable request to the Deputy Comptroller, Comptroller and possibly Legal (N00D).
steps.source_quote: Unusual or questionable requests are forwarded to the Deputy Comptroller, Comptroller, and possibly Legal (N00D)

steps.action: Reviews the unusual or questionable request before N8 takes action.
steps.source_quote: for review prior to taking action

steps.action: Checks whether funding is available for the request, using funds status from the Corporate Master Execution File Funds Status System.
steps.system: Corporate Master Execution File Funds Status System
steps.source_quote: If funding is available, routine requests are processed by assigning the appropriate LOA.

steps.action: Assigns the LOA and document number and provides them to the requestor and to the CH with a request to make the purchase.
steps.output: LOA, document number and purchase request to CH
steps.source_quote: The LOA and document number are provided to the requestor, and to the purchase card holder with a request to make the purchase.

steps.action: Forwards the requirement to the Comptroller for review when funding is exhausted.
steps.source_quote: If funding is exhausted, requirements are forwarded to the Comptroller for review.

steps.action: Completes the required documentation (SF 182 or NETC 4235/4), obtains approval signatures, and provides signed copies to N8 and the CH. Then proceeds to S29.
steps.source_quote: the requestor completes the required documentation, obtains the appropriate signatures for approval, and provides signed copies to N8 and the purchase card holder

steps.action: Prepares the SF 182 for its employee, assigning the LOA, stating in Section C that payment will be made with the GCPC, and annotating the CH's name and phone number (obtained from N4).
steps.source_quote: Each division prepares the SF 182 for their employees.

steps.action: Obtains the appropriate approval signatures on the SF 182.
steps.source_quote: Departments desiring training must complete SF 182 and obtain appropriate signatures for approval.

steps.action: Provides a copy of the SF 182 to N4.
steps.source_quote: Provide a copy of SF 182 to N4 prior to forwarding to Human Resources Office.

steps.action: Forwards the SF 182 to the Human Resources Office.
steps.source_quote: prior to forwarding to Human Resources Office

steps.action: Provides signed SF 182 copies to N8 and the CH so the purchase can be made. Then proceeds to S29.
steps.output: Authorized training purchase request to CH
steps.source_quote: Signed copies are provided to N8 and the purchase card holder so the purchase can be made.

steps.action: Provides a copy of the conference approval request, with a line of accounting specified, to N4.
steps.output: Approval request copy with LOA at N4
steps.source_quote: Departments desiring to sponsor a conference will provide a copy of the approval request to N4 ensuring that a line of accounting is specified.

steps.action: Reviews remaining funding at the end of the fiscal year.
Notifies the Division Directors/Special Assistants and asks for remaining unfunded requirements.
steps.source_quote: N8 notifies the Division Directors/Special Assistants asking for remaining unfunded requirements.

steps.action: Submit remaining unfunded requirements to N8.
Identifies funding for the requirements and notifies the departments, approving end-of-year purchases.
steps.source_quote: Once funding is identified, departments are notified.

steps.action: Ensures sufficient funds are committed by the R/FM before purchasing.
steps.source_quote: Ensure sufficient funds are committed by the R/FM.

steps.action: Screens the purchase request against mandatory supply sources (e.g., AbilityOne) and documents the screening in the purchase card log.
steps.source_quote: Screen the purchase request from mandatory supply sources (i.e., Ability One)

steps.action: Prepares the order through the mandatory source: office supplies from DoD EMALL or SERVMART using NETC 4400/1, and printing from DLA Document Services (DD Form 282). Then proceeds to AO approval (S33).
steps.source_quote: procure office supplies from DoD EMALL or SERVMART using NETC 4400/1. Procure printing requirements from DLA Document Services.

steps.action: Determines whether the merchant's price is fair and reasonable, rotating orders among qualified contractors as far as practicable.
steps.source_quote: Rotate orders among qualified contractors to the maximum extent practicable.

steps.action: Requests AO approval before purchasing.
steps.source_quote: Obtain AO approval prior to purchasing.

steps.action: Reviews and approves or rejects the proposed purchase.
steps.source_quote: responsible for ensuring proper use of the purchase card through approval of purchases

steps.action: Confirms the purchase complies with the delegated contract authority (single purchase, monthly and office limits; authorized transaction types) and is not a restricted item.
steps.source_quote: Comply with their delegated contract authority.

steps.action: Reviews the request to exceed the CH's single purchase limit.
steps.source_quote: The single purchase limit cannot be exceeded unless approved by N4.

steps.action: Places the order over the counter, by phone or via the internet, safeguarding the account. Reminds the merchant not to charge sales tax and seeks FOB destination terms.
steps.source_quote: CH may proceed to purchase the supplies

steps.action: Confirms the merchant agrees not to charge until shipment (or to bill only for quantities shipped), not to back order, to deliver within 30 days, and to put the required details on the packing list.
steps.source_quote: The CH must confirm that the merchant agrees

steps.action: Checks the transaction against the single purchase limit, billing cycle purchase limit, AO office limit, transaction method and merchant type, and grants or denies authorization.
steps.source_quote: the CITIBANK authorization system checks the CH's single purchase limit, the billing cycle purchase limit, the AO's billing cycle office limit

steps.action: Contacts the A/OPC about the denied transaction.
steps.source_quote: CHs must contact the A/OPC for denied transactions.

steps.action: Records the transaction in the purchase card log, keeping documentation that supports the decision to use the card and any special approvals.
steps.source_quote: A purchase card log, NETC 4430/1, is required to record all purchase card transactions.

steps.actor: Receiving/inspecting individual (not the CH who awarded)
steps.action: Receives and inspects the supplies or services, with legible signature and date.
steps.input: Delivered supplies or services; packing list
steps.source_quote: one will perform receipt/inspection

steps.action: Accepts the supplies or services, with legible signature and date.
steps.source_quote: These actions must be accomplished by legible signature and date.

steps.actor: Individual other than the person who placed the order
steps.action: In an emergent situation, performs the combined receipt, inspection and acceptance (two-way separation). Then proceeds to S45.
steps.source_quote: The individual responsible for the award of a contract or placement of an order will not perform the receipt, inspection, and acceptance function.

steps.action: Identify whether the material must be recorded in a formal property management or accounting system.
steps.source_quote: AOs and CHs identify whether materials need to be recorded in a formal property management or accounting system.

steps.action: Records the accountable property in DPAS, which N4 maintains.
steps.source_quote: All materials classified as accountable property will be recorded in the Defense Property Accounting System (DPAS).

steps.action: Provides a copy of the conference final bill to N4 once the conference is complete.
steps.source_quote: Provide a copy of the final bill to N4 upon completion of the conference.

steps.action: Closes the billing cycle and issues the monthly statement; its status changes from INTERIM to NEW.
steps.output: Monthly CH statement and billing statement
steps.source_quote: The billing cycle activity ends on the 19th of each month.

steps.action: Notifies the AO that the CH is not available to review the statement for certification.
steps.source_quote: Notify the AO if CH is not available to review the statement for certification.

steps.action: Reviews the absent CH's statement and documentation and certifies the account for payment.
steps.source_quote: The AO will review the CH's statement and documentation and certify the account for payment.

steps.action: Meets with the CH on their return to review the CH's statement.
steps.source_quote: The AO will meet with the CH upon their return to review the CH's statement.

steps.action: Verifies the accuracy of each transaction and ensures every purchase is in the purchase log and charged or reallocated to the proper LOA.
steps.source_quote: The CH will verify the accuracy of each transaction at the end of the monthly billing cycle.

steps.action: Uses pay-and-confirm for items billed but not received: confirms with the vendor that the items are in transit, reconciles and pays in full, and tracks the open transactions.
steps.source_quote: The CH will confirm with the vendor that the items ordered are in transit

steps.action: Uses pay-and-confirm for damaged items under warranty that the contractor will replace, modify or repair, keeping the transaction documentation in a suspense file until the transaction or credit posts.
steps.source_quote: The CH will retain the transaction documentation in a suspense file until the transaction or credit appears on the statement.

steps.action: Attaches an explanation for any transaction without documentation, giving item description, cost, transaction date, merchant name, price, quantity and the reason documentation is missing.
steps.source_quote: they must attach an explanation

steps.action: Certifies the bank statement and forwards all documentation to the AO/CO.
steps.source_quote: The CH will certify the bank statement and forward all documentation to the AO/CO.

steps.action: Reconciles the CH's statement in CITIBANK, confirms purchases were appropriate and charges accurate, verifies supporting documentation, and confirms receipt, inspection and acceptance (e.g., initials on each receipt).
steps.source_quote: Reconcile the CH's monthly statement in CITIBANK.

steps.action: Notifies the A/OPC or NETC N4 of a suspected unauthorized purchase (noncompliance, fraud, misuse or abuse). Then proceeds to S62.
steps.source_quote: Notify the A/OPC or NETC N4 in the event of any suspected unauthorized purchase

steps.action: Certifies the monthly invoice and forwards it to the appropriate office for payment.
steps.source_quote: The CO certifies the monthly billing statement and forwards it to the appropriate office for payment.

steps.action: Completes the monthly PAT review and returns all supporting documentation to the CH.
steps.output: Completed PAT review; documentation returned to CH
steps.source_quote: Complete the monthly PAT Review within 15 calendar days of the end of the billing cycle and return all supporting documentation to the CH.

steps.action: Notifies the A/OPC to resolve and reconcile the statement when the expected transactions or credits did not post on the next statement.
steps.source_quote: the CH or AO will notify the A/OPC to resolve and reconcile the statement

steps.action: Contacts the A/OPC to determine whether the Dispute or the Fraudulent Transaction procedure applies.
steps.source_quote: The CH or AO must contact the A/OPC to determine which procedure is appropriate

steps.action: Determines which single procedure (dispute or fraud) to start for the suspect transaction.
steps.source_quote: initiate only one procedure for a suspect transaction

steps.action: Disputes the transaction through the invoice certification process in CitiDirect; CitiDirect automatically short-pays the invoice by the disputed amount.
steps.source_quote: Transactions must be disputed through the invoice certification process within CitiDirect.

steps.action: Signs the CITIBANK Government Cardholder Dispute Form (Appendix B) and faxes or mails it to CITIBANK.
steps.system: Fax (605-357-2019) or mail; Appendix B form
steps.source_quote: submit/fax the CITIBANK Government Cardholder Dispute Form (Appendix B) to CITIBANK at 605-357-2019

steps.action: Tracks the dispute to resolution by calling CITIBANK or checking the dispute log in CitiDirect.
steps.source_quote: Track the dispute to resolution either by calling CITIBANK or reviewing the CITIBANK dispute log within CitiDirect.

steps.action: Resolves the dispute in favor of either the CH or the merchant.
steps.source_quote: the charge will either be resolved in favor of the CH or the merchant

steps.action: Offsets the charge with a bank chargeback or vendor credit, plus a debit (rebill) transaction to offset the short pay.
steps.source_quote: the charge is offset by either a vendor credit or bank initiated credit

steps.action: Sends the CH a letter explaining the decision; the charge is rebilled on the next invoice.
steps.source_quote: a letter will be sent to the CH explaining the decision

steps.action: Certifies the rebilled charge for payment on the next invoice.
steps.source_quote: the charge will appear in the balance due on the next invoice and must be certified for payment

steps.action: Notifies the A/OPC immediately of the suspected fraudulent activity.
steps.source_quote: The CH must notify the A/OPC immediately of any suspected fraudulent activity on the account.

steps.action: Contacts CITIBANK about the fraud.
steps.source_quote: The A/OPC will contact CITIBANK.

steps.action: Confirms with the CH which transactions are valid or fraudulent, closes the account, opens a replacement account with a new card, and moves the valid transactions to it.
steps.output: Closed account; new card; valid transactions moved
steps.source_quote: The bank will confirm with the CH which transactions are valid and which are fraudulent, close the account and move the valid transactions to the new card account.

steps.action: Short-pays the invoice by the fraudulent amount and certifies it through the manual certification process, not the dispute process.
steps.source_quote: certified using the manual certification process

steps.action: Completes the Declaration of Unauthorized Use form (Appendix C), submits it to the bank, and follows any further A/OPC guidance.
steps.source_quote: the CH will complete a Declaration of Unauthorized Use form (Appendix C) to be submitted to the bank

steps.action: Calls CITIBANK immediately to report the lost or stolen card.
steps.source_quote: the CH must immediately notify CITIBANK by calling 1-800-790-7206

steps.action: Notifies the AO and the A/OPC of the lost or stolen card.
steps.source_quote: The CH must also notify the AO and the A/OPC of a lost or stolen card within one business day after discovering the card missing.

steps.action: Submits a written report to the A/OPC (last six card digits, CH name, date and location of loss, police report date if stolen, time CITIBANK was notified, same-day purchases, other details).
steps.source_quote: The AO will submit a written report to the A/OPC within one business day.

steps.action: Mails a replacement card.
steps.source_quote: CITIBANK will mail a replacement card within one business day of the reported loss or theft.

steps.action: Cuts the found card in half and gives it to the AO or the A/OPC.
steps.source_quote: will be cut in half and given to their AO or the A/OPC

steps.action: Makes the departing CH's account inactive before departure.
steps.source_quote: the A/OPC shall ensure, to the maximum extent possible, that the CH account is inactive at least 30 days (one billing cycle) prior to departure

steps.action: Reduces the CH's single and monthly limits to $1.00 and cuts up the card to prevent further charges.
steps.source_quote: the A/OPC shall reduce the CH credit limits, as soon as practical, to $1.00 (single and monthly limits) and cut up the GCPC

steps.action: Closes the account once all transactions and payments have cleared.
steps.source_quote: The A/OPC will close the account once all transactions and payments have cleared.

steps.action: Turns in all files documenting GCPC transactions to the AO/CO for retention on leaving the command.
steps.source_quote: All files documenting GCPC transactions shall be turned in to the AO/CO for retention when a CH leaves the command.

steps.action: Retains the financial transaction records for audit per references (f) and (g).
steps.source_quote: be retained for a period of 10 years

steps.action: Conducts the monthly transaction review in PAT, covering internal controls, training, span of control and delinquencies; the review is automatically submitted to the next higher-level A/OPC.
steps.output: Monthly review submitted to next higher A/OPC
steps.source_quote: The A/OPC shall conduct a review of transactions using the DON Data Mining System PAT

steps.action: Conducts the semi-annual review, aggregating the previous six monthly reviews.
steps.system: DON Data Mining System PAT; Semi-Annual Review Auxiliary Worksheet (Appendix D)
steps.source_quote: The A/OPC shall conduct the semi-annual review using the approved DON Data Mining System PAT and the Semi-Annual Review Auxiliary Worksheet (Appendix D).

steps.action: Reviews and approves the semi-annual report.
steps.source_quote: The report shall be provided to the HA (N4) for review and approval.

steps.action: Forwards the approved semi-annual report to the Hierarchy Level 3 A/OPC (the SOP does not name who forwards it).
steps.source_quote: Upon approval, the report will be forwarded to the Hierarchy Level 3 A/OPC

steps.action: Compiles the report and submits it to CCPMD.
steps.source_quote: for compilation and submission to CCPMD

steps.action: Informs N4 of the upcoming 18-month Procurement Performance Management Assessment Program review by formal letter.
steps.source_quote: The analyst will inform N4 of the review by formal letter.

steps.action: Compiles the documents required for the review.
steps.source_quote: The A/OPC will compile the required documents for review and approval by the HA.

steps.action: Reviews and approves the review document package.
steps.source_quote: Upon HA approval

risks.description: Section 4.a lets the requesting department nominate a CH 'by email or memo' to the A/OPC. Nothing tracks whether the nomination arrived or how far onboarding has progressed.

Section 5.b says failing refresher training 'will result in suspension of account' but names no one to track the two-year deadlines or apply the suspension. The annual ethics (5.c) and annual CLG (5.d) deadlines also have no owner.
Training certificate copies go to the A/OPC (5.c(2)) with no stated method or tracking. That gap undermines the training gate before purchasing (4.a, 5.a).
Centrally managed requests are 'emailed to N8' (6.c) and referred onward to the Comptroller/Legal (S13) with no log, status or tracking.

Section 6.c routes 'unusual or questionable' requests to the Deputy Comptroller, Comptroller and 'possibly Legal'. It gives no criteria for what is unusual, does not say who decides on Legal, and sets no review timeframe.
Decision D3 has no stated next step when the Comptroller/Legal review does not clear the request (6.c).
Funds status updates are provided 'occasionally or upon request' (6.e), so N8's funding check may rely on stale data.
When funding is exhausted, requirements are forwarded to the Comptroller for review (6.e). No outcome or next step is stated.
Under 16.b the GCPC may not pay for SF 182 training over $25,000. The SOP gives no alternative route for such requests (decision D6 'No' branch).
The LOA and the CH's name and phone (obtained from N4) are typed onto the SF 182 (16.c). The same LOA is entered again in the purchase log and in the CitiDirect charge or reallocation (7.e, 10.a).
Signed SF 182 copies go separately to N4 (16.d), HRO (16.d), N8 and the CH (6.b). Nothing confirms that each copy was received or that N4 got its copy before HRO.
Section 6.f covers only the case where end-of-year funding is available. Decision D7 'No' has no stated handling.

Sections 6.a and 7.a(2) require funds committed by the R/FM before purchase, yet 6.a says 'specific dollar amounts are not assigned' and expenditures are only 'routinely monitored' by N8. No check or evidence of commitment is defined before money moves.
Decision D8 has no stated next step when sufficient funds are not committed (6.a, 7.a(2)).
Section 7.b only covers a fair and reasonable price. Decision D10 'No' has no next step, and the SOP does not require the price basis to be documented.

Section 7.a(3) requires AO approval before purchasing but sets no form, channel or record. Section 7.e expects documentation of 'any required special approvals', so the pre-approval may leave no audit trail.
Decision D11 has no stated next step when the AO does not approve the purchase (7.a(3)).
Section 12 lists restricted purchases 'but is not limited to' them and gives no alternative procurement route for restricted items.
Decision D13 has no next step when N4 does not approve exceeding the single purchase limit (8).
CHs must contact the A/OPC about denied transactions (19), but how the A/OPC resolves a denial is not stated.

Transactions are recorded in the NETC 4430/1 log, 'manual or automated' (2.l, 7.e), and then reconciled line by line against the same transactions in CitiDirect (10.a). Mandatory-source screening is logged separately (S30).
Section 9.b allows two-way separation 'in emergent situations' without defining emergent or naming who authorizes the reduced control.
Section 14 has AOs and CHs identify accountable property for N4 to record in DPAS. It sets no deadline and no handoff method, so items worth $5,000 or more, or pilferable items, may go unrecorded.
When the CH is unavailable, the AO alone reviews and certifies the statement for payment (10.a(3)). CH verification happens only after payment, at an unspecified 'upon their return' meeting.
The CH tracks billed but unreceived items with no stated tool (10.a(1)). Nothing ensures the dispute is filed inside the 60-day window from the statement date (11.a(5)).

Section 10 says the CH and AO/CO 'shall complete the reconciliation process within five business days' of INTERIM changing to NEW. Section 10.b(6) gives the AO/CO 10 business days from the same trigger to certify the monthly invoice.

The owner of suspected-fraud notification differs across sections. Section 10.b(4) has the AO/CO notify 'the A/OPC or NETC N4'. Section 11.b(1) says 'the CH must notify the A/OPC immediately'. Section 11 says 'the CH or AO must contact the A/OPC'.
Sections 3.c and 3.d state that the same person is both AO and CO, so one person approves purchases, verifies and certifies payment. No backup AO/CO is named to meet certification deadlines.
When pay-and-confirm transactions or credits do not post, the CH or AO notifies the A/OPC 'to resolve and reconcile' (10.a(2)). The resolution steps are not stated.

The A/OPC function is performed by the GCPC Program Manager (N4) at one listed number (3.b). Dispute and fraud determinations (11), fraud bank contact, lost-card reports (17), denials (19) and departures (20) all route to this role with no backup named.
Section 11.a says charges involving CH misuse or abuse are not disputable, but section 11 gives no alternative handling route.
The CH has 60 days from the statement date to dispute (11.a(5)). No handling is stated if the window is missed.
The dispute is entered in CitiDirect and then re-entered on the paper Appendix B form, which is faxed or mailed to CITIBANK (11.a(2)).
The SOP says 'Track the dispute to resolution' by calling CITIBANK or checking the log (11.a(3)), with no frequency and no explicit owner.
The section 17 introduction says 'CHs and AOs will contact CITIBANK' to report a lost or stolen card. Section 17.a assigns the immediate call to the CH alone.
The same loss details (card digits, dates, bank notification time) are given by phone to CITIBANK and in the CH notice. The AO then retypes them into a written report (17.b).
Section 20 defines no trigger telling the A/OPC that a CH is leaving, unlike 4.a for new participants. An account may stay active past departure, which section 20 prohibits.
Section 20 uses 'to the maximum extent possible' for inactivation and 'as soon as practical' for reducing limits to $1.00, with no firm deadline.
Section 21 requires files to be turned in when the CH leaves but sets no check that they were. The 10-year retention requirement depends on this step.
No next step is stated if the HA does not approve the semi-annual report (22.b, D28) or the external review package (23.a, D29).
Sections 22.b and 23.a say the report or package 'will be forwarded' without naming who forwards it. Section 23.a also uses an unspecified 'required date'.
Section 23.b does not name who suspends the accounts, or who selects the one CH and one AO account kept open for mission-essential needs.

starter_flows.trigger: When an item is created in the SharePoint 'GCPC Purchase Requests' list (CH submits the Power Apps purchase request form)
actions: Get the CH's record from the 'GCPC Cardholder Roster' list (AO, single purchase limit, monthly limit, authorized transaction types)
Get the related funding record (LOA and document number) and confirm the LOA field is populated; if blank, set status to 'Funding not confirmed' and notify the CH
Compare the request amount with the CH's single purchase limit and set an 'Exceeds limit' flag
Start and wait for the AO approval
If the AO approves and 'Exceeds limit' is true, start and wait for a second approval assigned to N4
Update the request status and record approver names, dates and comments for the audit trail (7.e)
Notify the CH of the outcome by Teams/Outlook; if approved, create a draft entry in the 'Purchase Card Log' list linked to the request
starter_flows.approval_step: Start and wait for an Approve/Reject approval assigned to the CH's AO. If the amount exceeds the single purchase limit, add a sequential approval assigned to N4 (section 8).

starter_flows.trigger: When an item is created or modified in the SharePoint 'Purchase Card Log' list (CH records the transaction in the Power Apps log form)
actions: Look up the linked purchase request and confirm it has an approved AO decision; if missing, flag the entry 'No pre-approval' and notify the A/OPC
Copy the LOA, document number, mandatory-source screening result and approvals from the request into the log entry
Calculate the billing cycle from the transaction date (cycle ends on the 19th, or the preceding Friday if the 19th falls on a weekend)
Check that a receipt is attached in the linked document library; if not, set a 'Receipt pending' reminder to the CH
Update the request status to 'Purchased'
Notify the designated receiving/inspecting person (not the CH) to complete receipt and inspection

starter_flows.trigger: When the CH sets the monthly 'Statement Reconciliation' item to 'CH Certified' in Power Apps
actions: Get all Purchase Card Log entries for the CH and billing cycle
For each entry, check for a receipt or a missing-documentation explanation (10.c) and for receipt/inspection and acceptance signatures (9.a)
If gaps are found, set status to 'Returned to CH', list the gaps and notify the CH
Compile the package as links to log entries and documents, and calculate deadlines from the INTERIM-to-NEW date (5 business days for reconciliation, 10 business days for certification)
Notify the AO/CO and start the review approval
